deviations.edit: Implemented all four plan nodes serially in the run root instead of fanning out to per-node git worktrees.
deviations.why: The fan-out path copies vendor/ and node_modules/ per node and runs the app bootstrap in each. For a change of this size (5 code files, ~90 lines) that cost exceeds the isolation benefit, and the driver already held verified grounding for every node. TDD discipline, the full-file blast-radius re-check, and a base-vs-change differential test run were all still performed.

deviations.edit: buildClickhouseQuery() filters org_id AND kit_id, not kit_id alone.
deviations.why: First cut replaced ->forOrg() with ->forKits(). org_id leads the scans_cold sort key (org_id, scanned_at, kit_id, id), so dropping it would have removed the primary-key pruning the ticket's whole 0.1-1.1s measurement depends on - a silent perf regression that could have reintroduced the timeout on ClickHouse. Caught before review; both filters are now applied, org first.

deviations.edit: retryUntil = 1 means ZERO retries, not one.
deviations.why: The driver told the operator that retryUntil=1 'keeps a single retry'. The real semantics are `if (retryCount >= retryUntil) stop`, so 1 stops on the first failure and 2 is what allows one retry. 1 was kept - it is what the ticket argues for ('retrying an unindexable scan unchanged cannot succeed') and it takes the log/metric amplification to 1x rather than ~2x - but the operator was told the wrong thing when they did not object, so it is recorded here and surfaced on the PR.

findings_fixed: R1-H1 Kit::getKits() projected only id+name, so ListScans::buildClickhouseQuery() emitted `org_id in (0)` - the ClickHouse Scans list would have returned ZERO rows for every user. Fixed by hydrating org_id; cache keys bumped to v2.

R1-H2 ScanVehicleController's ClickHouse branch filtered on scan_id alone on a route with no OrgMiddleware - a cross-tenant read that this diff would have promoted from staff-only to every authenticated user. Now kit-scoped, with an empty-kit short circuit.
R1-H4 stale org-kits: cache entries would have survived the H1 fix for up to an hour.
R1-M getSharedKits() passed a Collection nested in an array to whereIntegerInRaw.
R1-M lastFailureKey was never cleared on success, so a repeat failure of a previously-failed search was dropped from both log and metric.
R1-M retryUntil 1 -> reverted to 2: the trait is shared by four list pages and the amplification AC is met by the dedup guard alone.
R1-M the shape test asserted strpos ordering (certifies nothing) and never called buildClickhouseQuery() - rewritten to drive the real query through a booted page.
R2-REGRESSION ShareOrgKits forgot the pre-v2 cache key, so share/unshare stopped taking effect. Cache keys centralised behind Kit::kitsCacheKey()/sharedKitsCacheKey()/forgetCachedKits().

R2-H2 REGRESSION from the R1-H2 fix: getUserKits() defaults withShared:false while ListScans includes shared kits, so a shared-kit scan silently resolved no vehicle (and cached the empty result 15 min). Now getUserKits(withShared: true), pinned by a test that fails without it.
R2-M2 the dedup key now folds in the SQLSTATE so a DIFFERENT error on the same search still reports.
R2-L1 ShareOrgKits busts the kit cache once, not once per kit.
R2-L4 the retry fixture's mutable static is reset in tearDown().

The shared kit (id 16, owned by org 5) renders in the browser as 'QA DEV-2591 Shared Kit'. Generated ClickHouse SQL for the Scans page contains no FINAL; pinned by ClickhouseScanQueryShapeTest for both scans_cold and scans_hot.

Searches complete promptly with no timeout and no 'Search Criteria is too broad' empty state; Livewire round trip ~170-180ms server time. FlexSearch ON returning 0 rows for 'NA' is correct behaviour (it matches whole-plate OCR variants, not substrings) and is IDENTICAL on both paths, so it is not a divergence. Production-scale timing is the ticket's own read-only measurement (worst 1.11s warm / 3.12s cold vs a 20s timeout), not re-run here.

Verified by unit test rather than in the browser: a real SQLSTATE 57014 cannot be reproduced against the seeded local dataset. HasRetryQueryTest asserts one db-error entry + one clarity.query_timeout increment per distinct search, re-arming on a filter change, on a different SQLSTATE, and on success; plus a regression test proving alternating error codes still exhaust the retry budget.
'clarity.query_timeout drops to a level that reflects real distinct failures' is a post-deploy production observation. Deferred to the Datadog dashboard after release.
